title: Sheaves of modules on a small ringed site are Grothendieck abelian
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a site whose underlying category is small and let $\mathcal O$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$. The abelian category $\Mod(\mathcal O)$ of sheaves of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] is Grothendieck abelian [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian]: it has all small colimits, filtered colimits are exact, and the family of free sheaves $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ indexed by objects $U$ of $\mathcal C$ yields a generator $\bigoplus_{U\in\operatorname{Ob}\mathcal C}j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$, where $\mathcal O_U$ is the restriction of $\mathcal O$ to the localized site $\mathcal C/U$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] and $j_{U!}\mathcal O_U$ is the sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] of the extension-by-zero presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $P_{\mathcal O_U}$ [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf].

source.place: Section 07A5, first paragraph; Modules on Sites, Lemmas 03DA, 03DB, 03EW

proof.text: Apply the already proved SheafOfModules.isGrothendieckAbelian from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.Algebra.Category.ModuleCat.Sheaf.Abelian to the underlying sheaf of rings. This supplies all small colimits, exact filtered colimits, and a separator; Mathlib supplies abelianness [lem-pur-ringed-site-module-category-abelian].

Identify the free Yoneda presheaf with the explicit extension-by-zero presheaf of the localized unit [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] over [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. At V, use finsuppLEquivDirectSum to identify finitely supported functions on Hom(V,U) with the direct sum of copies of R(V). On a basis vector restriction in both constructions precomposes the index and takes coefficient 1 to 1. This proves naturality and gives a genuine presheaf isomorphism; applying module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] gives the sheaf isomorphism.

Use the source library theorem SheafOfModules.isSeparating_sheafification_freeYoneda. To test equality with each free Yoneda sheaf, precompose a test map with the inverse of the isomorphism from step 2, apply the localized-family hypothesis, and cancel the inverse. Apply ObjectProperty.IsSeparating.isSeparator_coproduct to the resulting separating family. Together with step 1 this proves both conjuncts with the original generator.
